Lesson 1 · Boundaries

A protocol gives a conversation a shape.

A protocol boundary separates an application-facing conversation from the tools and services an agent may use behind it.

Keep the layers distinct

The conversation protocol carries prompts, updates, and results. A tool protocol lets an agent call external capabilities. They can cooperate without becoming the same layer.

flowchart LR
  Client --> Agent
  Agent --> Tools

const result = await client.prompt(sessionId, content);
render(result.stopReason);
Example: conversation state

The client records which lesson is open while the agent responds through the agreed conversation interface.

Example: tool access

The agent may call a separate tool service, but that service does not own the learner conversation.

Example: a useful diagnostic

When something fails, first ask whether the conversation boundary or a downstream tool boundary failed.
